metadata.note: The Wabash Railroad and its successor-era operation by the Norfolk and Western, converted from research/branches/wabash_railroad.txt on 2026-09-28. Before this layer the map drew no Wabash route at all. Only the report's `drawable:` spans are drawn — never its pax_start / pax_end, which keep the wider unproven bracket. Every line still carrying passengers at the N&W lease (16 Oct 1964) is split into a Wabash feature and an N&W feature sharing identical geometry (Rule 4). The St. Louis, Kansas City & Northern, which ran the Missouri and Iowa lines until the November 1879 merger, is its own company in its own colour.

metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached tiles). Graph over every railway way (rail, abandoned, razed, disused, dismantled; streetcar and light rail excluded unless ex-Wabash); ways tagged old_railway_operator=Wabash cost 1x, untagged 1.25x, any other named operator 12x. Straight-line bridges only between dangling ends of abandoned or Wabash-tagged ways, priced 40x so they are used only where the grade is genuinely unmapped. Every feature's geometry_quality gives traced vs documented mileage, share on Wabash-tagged track, and each bridge.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS - these end years are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: Decatur - Hannibal, Keokuk Branch, Fort Wayne - Toledo, Moberly - Moulton and Moulton - Des Moines all stop at 1951 because the Feb 1952 Official Guide proves service then and no source dates the end; the Ottumwa Branch stops at 1893 and N&W Blanchard - Council Bluffs at 1966 for the same reason. The Decatur - Hannibal and Keokuk 1951 evidence rests on reading "Freight" trains with times in a public timetable as passenger-carrying; if that is rejected both collapse to 1875. Headways and speeds throughout are estimates. The Wabash's Ontario trackage-rights service (Detroit/Windsor - St. Thomas - Buffalo) has only one proven year, 1900, and is not drawn in this pass.
metadata.branches_deliberately_omitted: Per the report's drawable: NONE, or not drawn here: Streator, Effingham and Altamont branches (no Wabash-era passenger year; their 1875 Chicago & Paducah anchors are a different company); Moberly - Hannibal (freight-only by 1951 at least Monroe City - Moberly; no Wabash-era year); Salisbury - Glasgow; Edwardsville - Alton (1913 anchor, operator uncertain); Wabash Pittsburgh Terminal (separate company); Gould-era leased lines 1879-89 (Champaign - Havana, Rantoul narrow gauge, Lafayette - Bloomington, Decatur - Peoria, Indianapolis - Michigan City, Cairo - Danville, TP&W and others: no Wabash-era year, or low confidence on operator). Traced but not drawn: Chicago - Gary (1898 anchor only; its route over the C&WI and terminal roads could not be traced with confidence) and the Olive Street - Ferguson suburban loop (1887-1914; the loop via Baden is lifted and unmapped, and the trace fell onto the main line). The main-line St. Louis suburban service 1887-1907 shares the St. Louis - Kansas City geometry and is not a separate feature.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: From the Feb 1952 Guide "Freight Service only" tables and Index daggers: Sidney - Champaign, Maysville - Pittsfield, Quincy - Hannibal, Montpelier - Toledo, Monroe City - Moberly. In each case the passenger end is unknown and before 1951.
